content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I need to develop a small project using [product_name] [version_no]. Although the project seems straightforward at first, there are additional details where I could use some assistance. We have two flow meters: meter A with a maximum flow rate of 1000 m3/h, delivering 1 impulse for every 1 m3/h, and meter B with a flow rate of 100 impulse/h, where 1 m3/h equals 10 impulses. The logic should allow switching between meter A and meter B (or vice versa), depending on user settings, which can be configured via the [product_name] [version_no] operator interface as a percentage. For example, if meter A drops below 80% of its max capacity (meaning it operates at only 20%), the system should switch to meter B, which provides finer measurements. When meter B reaches a user-defined maximum, say 85%, it should switch back to meter A. The time delay for switching (hysteresis) should also be easily set by the user on the [product_name] operator panel, adjustable from 5 to 30 minutes. There is no external DAC available—I need to implement everything using the [product_name]. The operator panel should display both the actual flow in m3 and as a percentage. Given the slow impulse rates (e.g., meter A generates about 17–20 impulses per minute), what is the best way to count and process this data? Since quick reaction time isn't required, an integration period of 1–5 minutes is sufficient (user adjustment optional, but not strictly necessary). I appreciate any helpful suggestions or example solutions.

analysis.insight_summary: The user aims to create a control system using [product_name] and [product_name] operator panel that automatically switches between two flow meters based on set thresholds, with user-friendly adjustment options. The main challenge involves managing slow pulse rates for accurate, real-time measurement and ensuring that users can easily set parameters like switching thresholds and hysteresis via the operator panel.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects an intuitive interface, allowing easy adjustment of switching thresholds and hysteresis time through the [product_name] operator panel, as well as clear, real-time display of measured values. Additionally, they want reliable handling of slow impulse rates to ensure accurate control logic.
